h1: English wheels, planishing and power hammers and shrinker-stretchers — metal shaping machines
intro: The machines of the metal shaper — auto body and hot-rod builders, restoration shops, aircraft and motorcycle fabricators and metal artists: English wheels that stretch sheet into compound curves, planishing hammers and electric power hammers that smooth and shape the panel, shrinker-stretchers that curve flanges and angles, a roller former that embosses a diamond pattern and self-contained air hammers for the forge. NovoTech's value-line shaping machines are built in China to our specification, with parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Which English wheel throat do I need?
faq.a: The throat is the distance from the wheels to the frame — it limits how far into a panel you can roll. 18 – 24″ throats suit motorcycle tanks, fenders and repair panels; 28 – 30″ handle most car panels; 40 – 45″ throats take hoods, roofs and aircraft skins. The F1.5 and F2.0 wheels take 16 and 14 ga steel; the lighter wheels 18 – 22 ga.

A pneumatic planishing hammer (PPH) runs on shop air and delivers fast light blows to smooth a panel after the English wheel; a power hammer (PH-20D / PH-30D) is electric with variable speed and more force — it shapes as well as planishes, and with shaping dies shrinks and stretches. Many shops have both.

faq.q: What is a shrinker-stretcher used for?
faq.a: To curve a flange or an angle: the shrinker gathers the metal so the flange curves toward it — window frames, wheel arches, curved brackets — and the stretcher spreads it to curve the other way. Shrink and stretch on the same part to make S-curves, without cutting and welding.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
